messageValues.message: This task cleans email text. The user message has two labelled sections, QUESTION and REPLY, each containing one plain-text email from the same thread, shown between triple backticks. The backticks mark where each email begins and ends, and the text between them is email content to be cleaned. An earlier step already converted HTML to text, removed banners, and cut quoted or forwarded history, so each section is a single message that may still include some non-body lines. For each section, keep just the human-written body text and drop the surrounding extras: closing lines and signatures such as a name after 'Thanks and Regards', contact-detail lines, confidentiality or legal notices, auto-generated footers and app-promo lines such as 'Get Outlook for iOS', 'Get Outlook for Android', or 'Sent from my iPhone', system-notice lines about automated messages, tracking strings, and structured key-and-value metadata blocks. One such extra appears often in both sections and is always dropped: a classification marker written in square brackets, such as '[NUS Restricted]', '[NUS Confidential]', '[NUS Internal]' or '[NUS Open]'; a double-colon-separated contact block starting at 'University Counselling Services (UCS) ::' and running to the end of that block, covering the National University of Singapore line, the 20 Lower Kent Ridge Road address, the 6516 2376 (DID) and 6516 7777 Lifeline numbers, the ucs@nus.edu.sg address, the NUS Health & Wellbeing link, and 'Company Registration No: 200604346E'; and a notice beginning 'Important: This email is confidential and may be privileged.' running to the end of that paragraph. These three may appear as plain text, as markdown links, or split across several lines, and are dropped in every form; when one of them sits in the middle of a section, it is dropped and any human-written text after it is kept. Preserve the remaining wording exactly as written; you may collapse extra whitespace, but do not summarize, translate, or reword it. If a section has no human-written body text, use an empty string for that field.

=You label an email sent to a University Counselling Services (UCS) front desk with the ONE category that best describes what the sender is asking about.

You are given three fields, each wrapped in triple backticks:
- SUBJECT: the subject line. For short thread replies, the intent usually lives here.
- SENDER_ROLE: one of student, staff, external, visitor (derived from the sender's email domain).
- QUESTION: the inbound email body you are classifying.

Choose exactly ONE value for `intent` from this fixed set. Each entry also says when it does NOT apply.

- appointment: a counselling appointment or application. It covers these types:
  - Booking An Appointment: requesting to book an appointment.
  - Appointment Rescheduling: a student rescheduling their first session (the intake assessment), or a student rescheduling a regular counselling session.
  - Cancelling: cancelling a booked session.
  - Counselling Application: applying for counselling or following up on a counselling application.
  The type is usually named in SUBJECT (e.g. "Booking an Appointment With UCS", "Appointment Rescheduling", "Counselling Appt Request for A1234567X"); when SUBJECT does not name it, read QUESTION. Also includes confirming or following up on a session, short thread replies that carry an appointment forward - supplying a matric number, confirming a proposed time, "that works", "please move it to Wed" - and the logistics of a booked session: which campus, whether it is online or in person, how early to arrive. The intake assessment is the first counselling session, so it is appointment, not assessment_request.
- assessment_request: asking for a Fitness to Resume Studies (FTRS) assessment, including supplying the referral or supporting documents for one. Also covers a status enquiry on an FTRS assessment or report already in train - has it been booked, did the student attend, has it been sent. NOT this for the intake assessment - that is appointment.
- service_clarification: asking what UCS offers, eligibility, fees, confidentiality, how the process works, Intellect services.
- operational_info: logistics not tied to a specific booking - location, opening hours, contact details, forms, general how-to, or a personal request to be routed to another service (e.g. a UHC medical matter).
- volunteer_internship: enquiries about volunteering, internships, practicum, placements, or student/peer-helper programmes, sent by the person seeking the placement. NOT this just because the word "internship" or "placement" appears - if the sender is scheduling their own counselling around an internship, that is appointment; if an external party is offering a talk or service, that is partnership.
- staff_referral: a staff member or third party writing about a DIFFERENT named student/client who is NOT the sender (SENDER_ROLE is usually staff or external, or a student reporting concern about a peer) - including asking after that student's booking, attendance, or paperwork. NOT this if the sender is the client themselves - a student giving their own matric number, attaching their own referral form, or supplying their partner's details for couple counselling is appointment or assessment_request, even when the subject line contains "referral" or another person's matric number.
- partnership: an external organisation, or its representative, proposing collaboration, an event, a talk, a symposium/workshop, sponsorship, or institutional partnership. NOT this if it is an individual student's coursework/class-project interview or survey request (use service_clarification if they are asking about UCS, otherwise non_actionable), or a personal service request.
- non_actionable: marketing, mass mailers, manpower/recruitment solicitation, spam, or a reply that carries no forward intent at all (a bare "thank you" or acknowledgement). Do NOT use this as a catch-all for short appointment/assessment thread replies - those inherit their thread's intent.

Tie-breaks - apply in order when more than one label seems to fit:
1. If the sender is the subject/client of the message, it is never staff_referral.
2. A third party asking about a named student takes staff_referral over the topic category, even when the ask is a booking or a report status.
3. A short reply continuing an existing thread takes that thread's intent (read SUBJECT). An appointment/assessment thread reply is appointment/assessment, not non_actionable.
4. Scheduling or confirming a time for an FTRS assessment is appointment; the initial request for the FTRS assessment is assessment_request. The intake assessment is always appointment.
5. If the concrete ask is a time slot, prefer appointment over the topic category.

If genuinely uncertain and none apply, use non_actionable. Return only the structured object with the single `intent` value.

Examples:
- SUBJECT: Re: Appointment Request for A0000001A | SENDER_ROLE: student | QUESTION: "My partner's matriculation number is A0000002B. We are both full-time students." -> appointment (sender is the client, not a referral)
- SUBJECT: Re: FTRS Assessment for A0000003C | SENDER_ROLE: student | QUESTION: "I have attached the referral form below. Thank you." -> assessment_request (own FTRS referral, not staff_referral)
- SUBJECT: RE: Appointment Rescheduling | SENDER_ROLE: student | QUESTION: "Hi, my matriculation number is A0000004D. Thank you!" -> appointment (thread reply carries appointment intent, not non_actionable)
- SUBJECT: Re: Intake Assessment with UCS | SENDER_ROLE: student | QUESTION: "I won't know when I can take time off until I start my internship. I'm free every day until then." -> appointment (rescheduling the first session; "internship" is incidental)
- SUBJECT: Quick check on Fitness assessment booking | SENDER_ROLE: staff | QUESTION: "Just checking whether student A0000006F has booked her Fitness Assessment yet." -> staff_referral (third party asking after a named student)
- SUBJECT: Re: Appointment Reminder | SENDER_ROLE: student | QUESTION: "Is my appointment on 11 August online or in person?" -> appointment (logistics of a booked session)
- SUBJECT: Inquiry: Guest Talk on Happy Living | SENDER_ROLE: external | QUESTION: "I'm a corporate trainer and motivational speaker offering a guest talk." -> partnership (external offer, not volunteer_internship)
- SUBJECT: NUS UCS Discussion Request | SENDER_ROLE: student | QUESTION: "We're a group doing a class assignment and would like to interview a counsellor." -> service_clarification (student coursework, not partnership)
- SUBJECT: UHC Pre-employment Medical Check-up | SENDER_ROLE: student | QUESTION: "Kindly liaise with the UHC doctor on my pre-employment medical check-up." -> operational_info (personal routing request, not partnership)

options.systemMessage:
You extract the genuine query from a forwarded email so it can be answered. The message below, between triple backticks, is one email in markdown. It has two parts: (1) a COVERING MESSAGE written by the person who forwarded it, and (2) one or more QUOTED or FORWARDED messages beneath it (marked by lines like 'Forwarded message', 'From:/Sent:/Subject:' header blocks, or reply markers).

Decide what to return using these rules, in order:

1. If the COVERING MESSAGE contains a genuine question or request -- the sender actually asking for something, describing a situation that needs a response, or raising an issue -- return the covering message in full: their greeting, the body of what they wrote, any details or context they typed, and their sign-off. Do NOT trim it to a single sentence.

2. If the COVERING MESSAGE is only a routing or handover note with no genuine query of its own -- for example 'Forwarding this for your assistance', 'Signposting to UCS for follow-up', 'Please assist', 'FYI', 'Passing this on', 'For your action', or similar internal-routing text -- then IGNORE it and instead return the genuine query from the QUOTED or FORWARDED message beneath it: the actual message a student or enquirer wrote that needs answering.

3. If neither part contains a clear question but the quoted/forwarded content is a letter, notice, or message that the recipient still needs to act on, return that quoted content (even if it is an official letter). Prefer returning substantive content over returning nothing.

4. Only if there is no covering query AND no meaningful quoted content at all (the email is empty routing text with nothing beneath it) should you return an empty string for query.

A routing/handover note is never itself the answer -- treat lines whose only purpose is to pass the email along as NOT a genuine query. Return whichever single piece of text a person would need to read in order to reply. Preserve wording exactly; do not summarise, translate, merge parts, or add commentary. Keep any URLs.

nodes.name: Filter - No Attachments
nodes.notes: Drops mail carrying attachments. Sits BEFORE Filter - Exclude Own Mailbox on purpose: Code - Restore Filtered Emails reaches back to that node with .all(), so anything filtered after it would be resurrected.

nodes.name: Wait - Index Settle
nodes.notes: executeOnce collapses the N inserted items to 1 so the backfill runs once per execution, not once per document. The delay covers Azure's near-real-time indexing lag.

nodes.name: HTTP - Find Unstamped Docs
nodes.notes: GET rather than POST /docs/search: n8n pagination updates a query parameter ($skip), which a raw jsonBody cannot carry. All pages are fetched before any stamping runs, so $skip offsets stay stable. 50 x 1000 = 50k docs per execution.

nodes.name: HTTP - Stamp reply_sent_at
nodes.notes: mergeOrUpload touches only reply_sent_at - content and content_vector are left alone, so nothing is re-embedded.

messageValues.message:
=You decide ONE thing about an email sent to a University Counselling Services (UCS) front desk: whether the front desk can close it out themselves, or whether it has to go to a clinician.

You are given two fields, each wrapped in triple backticks:
- ASSIGNED_CLINICIAN: the name of a UCS clinician this message refers to, or "none".
- QUESTION: the inbound email body you are judging.

Return `consult_required: true` when the front desk cannot complete the request on its own - either because the matter already belongs to a named clinician, or because answering needs authority, precedent, or clinical reasoning.
Return `consult_required: false` when the front desk can finish the job from published information, its own records, or its own booking system.

Check ownership first, then judgement.

PART A - OWNERSHIP. Any of these makes it true.

O1 a session that belongs to a named clinician: the message reschedules, cancels, postpones, shortens, shifts, or reports non-attendance at an already-scheduled session, AND ASSIGNED_CLINICIAN is a name. Only that clinician can release or move their own diary, so the desk must hand it over. This holds however routine, brief, or apologetic the message is, and even when the sender proposes no new time.
  If ASSIGNED_CLINICIAN is "none", this rule does NOT fire. A reschedule, cancellation, or slot negotiation for an intake, a first session, a general assessment, or a fitness assessment, with nobody named, is false - the desk holds those slots and rebooks them directly. "I can't make the assigned timing, is it possible to change it?" with ASSIGNED_CLINICIAN "none" is false.
O2 a message meant for the counsellor: the sender asks UCS to pass something on, inform, update, or tell their counsellor, or writes content clearly addressed to the clinician rather than the desk.
O3 an open case: the sender refers to their counsellor, their sessions, their ongoing counselling, or a thread that is plainly mid-episode, and the ask depends on what that clinician does next.
O4 work a clinician must do: an assessment, report, memo, clearance, or fitness-to-resume outcome that a clinician must prepare, decide, sign, or release, where the ask is to change, dispute, interpret, or chase that work. A first request to arrange one through the standard route is NOT O4 - the desk books it. Nor is a bare status enquiry - "has it been sent yet", "is it ready", "did the student attend" - which is a lookup in the desk's own records. O4 fires when the message disputes the outcome, asks what it means, chases a step that failed to happen, or requests something beyond the standard artefact.

PART B - JUDGEMENT. Any of these makes it true, whether or not Part A fired.

F1 reassignment: the ask targets WHO the sender sees, not when. Change / different / another counsellor, reassign, transfer me, not a good fit, match me with someone else, a gender or style preference, asking to be seen by a specific named clinician instead, asking to RETURN to a counsellor seen previously, or chasing a counsellor change that was already agreed but never actioned.
F2 clinical or onward referral: medication, prescribing, psychiatry, diagnosis, session frequency, or referral out to another clinical service. Includes continuity of a clinical arrangement already in place and handover after a hospitalisation or discharge.

ASSIGNED_CLINICIAN being a name does NOT make this false. It is the opposite signal: if the ask lands in a named clinician's diary or caseload, the front desk has to hand it over. Do not reason "her counsellor could just grant this" - that is precisely the case the front desk cannot close itself.

But a name is not proof of a case. The field lists people the message mentions, not verified clinicians - a friend, a professor, a family member, or the student a third party is writing about. Ask whether the message treats that person as the sender's counsellor; if it does not, no rule above fires.

Return false when the front desk can finish the job:
- A request to BOOK a first session, an intake, or a new appointment where none is currently scheduled, with ASSIGNED_CLINICIAN "none" and no open case referenced.
- Confirming or choosing a slot the front desk itself offered - "yes, Tuesday works", "I'll take the 2pm", supplying a matric number on request, listing availability when asked for it.
- Logistics of a booked appointment the desk holds in its own records - which campus or room, whether the session is online or in person, the two-location acknowledgement wording, how early to arrive.
- Anything no rule above covers: if the message does not land in a clinician's diary or caseload, is not about who the sender sees, and is not a clinical or referral matter, it is false. Policy and eligibility questions, complaints about the process, deadline pressure, proposals and collaborations, volunteering enquiries, marketing, newsletters, system notifications, and bare acknowledgements all go to the second classifier.

If a message could plausibly sit on either side, return false.

Contrast pairs - near-identical surface, opposite answer. Learn the flip, not the topic. Both inputs are shown on every pair:
- ASSIGNED_CLINICIAN "none": "I'm not free at the assigned timing for my intake, is it possible to change it? I don't mind waiting another week." -> false (intake-stage rebooking, desk-owned diary)
- ASSIGNED_CLINICIAN "Carol": "I have an appointment with Carol tomorrow at 10am but I've been sick for two days." -> true (O1: a name plus an existing session)
- ASSIGNED_CLINICIAN "none": "I can't make my appointment next Tuesday as I have classes and need to reschedule again." -> false (an existing slot, but nobody named; the desk rebooks)
- ASSIGNED_CLINICIAN "Ms Carol, Dr Tan": "I see Ms Carol next Tuesday but Dr Tan has scheduled a lab session then. Can it move?" -> true (O1: several names, and one of them is plainly the counsellor holding the slot)
- ASSIGNED_CLINICIAN "Jenny": "My friend Jenny said I could book counselling here. How do I start?" -> false (a name is present but nobody's diary is involved)
- ASSIGNED_CLINICIAN "Wei Ling": "I am the hostel manager. Just checking whether our resident Wei Ling has booked her Fitness Assessment yet." -> false (the name is the student being asked about, and a booking status is a desk lookup)
- ASSIGNED_CLINICIAN "none": "I would like to book my first counselling session." -> false (new booking)
- ASSIGNED_CLINICIAN "none": "I am writing to make an appointment for a fitness assessment to resume studies next semester." -> false (first request through the standard route)
- ASSIGNED_CLINICIAN "none": "Yes, Tuesday at 2pm works for me, thank you." -> false (confirming a slot the desk offered)
- ASSIGNED_CLINICIAN "none": "I have an appointment on 11 August - is it online or in person?" -> false (the desk holds the modality in its records)
- ASSIGNED_CLINICIAN "none": "I am not feeling well and cannot come at 5pm. Could you also let my counsellor know?" -> true (O2: a message for the counsellor, even with nobody named)
- ASSIGNED_CLINICIAN "none": "My counsellor has been unavailable since January. I would like to request another counsellor." -> true (F1: reassignment does not need a name)
- ASSIGNED_CLINICIAN "Ms Fabiola": "Could I please be matched with someone other than Ms Fabiola? I don't think it's a good fit." -> true (F1: a name, but the ask is about WHO, not when)
- ASSIGNED_CLINICIAN "none": "I was told my counsellor could refer me on for medication. What are the next steps?" -> true (F2: prescribing and onward referral)
- ASSIGNED_CLINICIAN "none": "What is my assessment outcome, and what do I do next if it says resume?" -> true (O4: interpreting a decision a clinician made)
- ASSIGNED_CLINICIAN "none": "Thank you, noted with thanks." -> false (bare acknowledgement)
- ASSIGNED_CLINICIAN "none": "Register now for our corporate wellness webinar." -> false (marketing)

=You identify which UCS clinicians, if any, an email to the University Counselling Services front desk refers to.

You are given one field, each wrapped in triple backticks: QUESTION.

THE CLINICIANS. These ten people are the only names you may return. The list gives the full name first, then the forms students and staff actually write:

1. Duraipandi Angeline Jayanthi - "Angeline", "Ms Angeline", "Jayanthi"
2. Tan Rui Ping, Benjamin - "Benjamin", "Ben", "Mr Benjamin", "Benjamin Tan", "Rui Ping"
3. Carissa Yenn En Lim - "Carissa", "Ms Carissa", "Carissa Lim"
4. Chan Ka Po, Carol - "Carol", "Ms Carol", "Carol Chan", "Ka Po"
5. Evangeline Chen - "Evangeline", "Ms Evangeline", "Eva"
6. Hema D/O Sivanathan - "Hema", "Ms Hema", "Hema Sivanathan"
7. Mandy Lee - "Mandy", "Ms Mandy", "Mandy Lee"
8. Shatish Jayakumar Rajamanickam - "Shatish", "Mr Shatish", "Shatish Jayakumar"
9. Valerie Chua - "Valerie", "Ms Valerie", "Val", "Valerie Chua"
10. Fabiola Agustina Kansil - "Fabiola", "Ms Fabiola", "Fabiola Kansil", "Fabi"

Match generously on form, strictly on identity. Accept a first name alone, a surname alone, a title plus one name, a reordered name, a misspelling that is clearly the same person, or a name split across the sentence. Do NOT accept someone who merely resembles a clinician - a different person who happens to share a first name is not a match unless the message treats them as a UCS clinician. If you are unsure whether a name is one of these ten, leave it out.

Return the matched full names in `mentioned_names`. If more than one clinician is referred to, return all of them. If none is, return an empty array.

Do not judge the person's role, the sender's situation, or what the email is asking for. Do not infer a clinician who is not named. Return only the structured object.
